validity.recommendation: Re-verify Diameter with SNGPL directly (or an OGRA/annual-report primary source) before citing 8 in as settled. Independent 2018 press confirms this corridor exists and is SNGPL-operated, but describes a 12-inch pipe tied into the Abbottabad 'mega supply line' feeding Mansehra -- that may be (a) a later upgrade/second diameter on the same 70.53 km trunk (several roster rows carry multi-value Diameter, e.g. P4019 '20, 18', P4021 '12, 18, 20' -- this row plausibly should too), or (b) a separate, not-yet-catalogued distribution lateral off the trunk, in which case GEM's single 8 in figure for the trunk itself could still stand. Could not disambiguate from open sources; flagging rather than silently keeping 8 in or silently changing it to 12 in.
validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt this run (per scope note) and has zero Wayback snapshots (checked both the direct availability API and a CDX search -- no captures exist), so there is nothing of the sheet's own sourcing to re-verify; this is genuinely new research, not re-verification. wiki_citations.json has no entry for P4175, confirming the harvest never got in. All 6 non-owner fields (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Length, Diameter, Location) plus the owner ref came back MISSING_REF -- consistent with the scope note that this batch is a single bulk load from 2023-07-11 with no refs at all. EXISTENCE: found one clearly independent, non-GEM source -- The News International, 'Mansehra linked to 12-inch diameter gas pipeline' (dated Tue Feb 7 2018; live URL now 403s but a Wayback capture is live and passes url_verifier). It quotes an SNGPL officer (Hasham Khan) stating SNGPL 'linked Mansehra with 12 inches diameter pipeline' that was 'linked with mega supply line in Abbottabad,' bringing gas relief to Mansehra's CNG/commercial/domestic consumers. This independently confirms: (1) the pipeline is real, physically built infrastructure, not a database phantom; (2) SNGPL is the operator/owner, matching GEM's Owner1; (3) a Haripur-Abbottabad-Mansehra gas corridor exists and functions, consistent with GEM's Haripur->Mansehra routing (Haripur sits just north of Wah/Taxila on the way to Abbottabad and then Mansehra along the Hazara/KKH corridor -- straight-line driving distance Haripur-Mansehra is ~64 km per generic distance sites, plausibly close to the pipeline's stated 70.53 km once road/valley routing is accounted for). A second Wayback-archived URL from the same paper (print/277849) turned out to be the identical wire text republished under a different print ID, not an independent second source, so I am NOT double-counting it -- tier is medium (one strong, clearly independent source), not high. Could not find a second, distinct independent source after extensive searching (SNGPL annual report 2023 PDF text-searched for 'Haripur'/'Mansehra' -- only address-book hits for the Abbottabad regional office, no segment-level pipeline table; OGRA's site 403'd; two SNGPL tender PDFs referencing Abbottabad-region ditching work near Mansehra Road were located via search but failed url_verifier (200 but the expected 'Mansehra'/'Abbottabad' text was not extractable from the PDF, likely an image/scanned tender notice) so they are NOT cited; DuckDuckGo HTML search got rate-limited/CAPTCHA'd partway through, capping further attempts). CLASSIFICATION: transmission is consistent with how the dataset treats every other short (50-100 km, 8-24in) city-linking segment in this same Hazara/KP batch (P4176-P4182, P5486), so this is not a P4175-specific misclassification -- it is the dataset's convention for these trunk-to-city feeders, and the 2018 article's own language ('mega supply line') supports transmission-grade infrastructure rather than a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-pipeline roster -- no other row names Haripur or Mansehra, and the nearest geographic analogues (Wah-Nowshera I/II P4170/P4173, Rawat-Murree P4165, Dakhni-Meyal-Dhulian P4163) run west toward Peshawar or south toward Rawalpindi, not north into the Hazara corridor -- no plausible duplicate/relabel identified. SPEC (Length): 70.53 km is geographically plausible (see distance note above) but no independent source gives an exact km figure, so it remains unconfirmed rather than verified -- left as UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a ref. Net: existence, operator, and status are corroborated; the diameter figure is the one genuine open question, hence concern_type=spec rather than existence/duplicate/classification.

summary: P4175 Haripur-Mansehra Gas Pipeline: existence, SNGPL ownership, and operating status independently corroborated (medium tier, one strong 2018 press source, via Wayback since thenews.com.pk and gem.wiki both 403); flagged spec concern on Diameter (source describes a 12in pipe vs GEM's 8in -- ambiguous whether same asset or a separate lateral, not resolved); Length left unresolved (no independent km figure, only distance plausibility); no duplicate or classification problem found against the 63-pipeline roster.
